thread:
aj: Hey team, customer on paid plan reports intermittent failures when they set response_format=structured & strict=true. Sometimes works, sometimes we return an HTML error page and their parser dies. Seen across EU region.

maria: Thanks AJ — any repro or headers?

aj: Pasting their simplified curl + response snippet. Happens ~1/50 calls.

aj: ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-cust-XXXXX' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"rw-1.2","prompt":"...","response_format":"structured","strict":true}'
```

aj: Response sometimes: HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8

<html>...gateway error...</html>

aj: Other times we get proper JSON. Customer sees their parser throw and they escalate to billing because tokens still consumed.

maria: Hm. Does the response have any X-Request-ID or upstream code?

aj: They provided logs: X-Req: rq_abc123, Upstream-Err: 502 from model-host-12, but our runtime returned 200 HTML from the fallback page.

support-bot: Incident detection: possible transient auth rotation observed for customer tenant cust-6712 at 2024-11-05T14:22Z.

aj: Also noted that around the same time their billing system rotated API tokens (their side) via webhook. Not sure if related.

devin: Likely two separate issues that interact: 1) transient 5xx from model host leading to fallback page (HTML) 2) auth/token rotation that produced 401 which earlier logic may convert into non-JSON body.

sam: Can we confirm strict enforcement path? If strict=true we should reject non-JSON with 415 or 422, not return an HTML 200.

maria: Agreed — customer should get a structured error response when response_format is structured+strict. Need to reproduce.

aj: Repro steps customer gave: run high-volume calls with response_format=structured and occasionally see HTML. They shared a minimal script that triggers it after ~300 calls.

aj: ```python
# loop.py
import requests
for i in range(1000):
  r = requests.post('https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate', json={
    'model':'rw-1.2','prompt':'x','response_format':'structured','strict':True
  }, headers={'Authorization':'Bearer sk-cust-XXXXX','Accept':'application/json'})
  if 'html' in r.text.lower():
    print('FOUND HTML at', i, r.status_code, r.headers.get('Content-Type'))
    break
```

devin: Good. I'll try to replay with their API key in staging (with their permission) and toggle a proxy to simulate a 502 from model-host and a 401 from auth service at different times.

sam: In the meantime, can support ask for the exact raw response bytes for one of the failing requests (base64) plus X-Req? That helps trace which service returned HTML.

aj: Sent request to customer for raw capture + X-Req. They returned 2 captures. Attached summaries: one capture shows 200 + text/html + body with our internal fallback message; headers show X-Fallback-Reason: upstream-5xx.

maria: Ok X-Fallback-Reason header is key. That means our runtime saw upstream 5xx and chose to render fallback UI page (we have that behavior for human-facing paths). But API should not return UI. Looks like a routing bug where API traffic hit the UI fallback handler.

sam: That would explain HTML 200. Why would API traffic hit UI handler? Possibly header stripping during a proxy error or misrouted request after auth rotation. If auth returns 401 we have code path that redirects to login page in UI host. Need to check.

devin: Action plan: (1) reproduce in staging by injecting 502 from model host; (2) check router rules for fallback when Accept includes application/json vs browser Accept; (3) audit codepath when auth returns 401 for API token—should respond 401 JSON, not redirect or HTML.

maria: Quick fix: change API gateway to prefer content-negotiation: if Accept contains application/json or response_format=structured, force error JSON from fallback. Sam can we ship a short config bump to enforce that?

sam: I can deploy a patch to router to honor Accept header on fallback. Will push a canary to EU region. ETA ~45m.

aj: Customer update queued: told them we're investigating, asked for raw traces. They are surprised because billing charged tokens on failures. They've paused traffic for now.

support-bot: Note: billing-team notified (ticket #BILL-9876).

maria: Also need to verify that strict=true triggers 422 on non-JSON. If current code returns 200 HTML then strict enforcement is broken. Add unit test for strict mode.

devin: I'll add regression test and a monitoring alert: any API response with Content-Type not application/json for requests with response_format structured to increment a metric.

sam: Canary deployed to eu-west-1 with Accept-aware fallback. I'll report back in 20m.

aj: Customer replied with one more raw capture; X-Req: rq_def456, shows 200 html at 2024-11-05T14:22:18Z. Forwarded to devin.

devin: Replayed rq_def456 in staging. Confirmed that the error originated in the model-host returning 502, our router forwarded to fallback UI handler because the auth middleware saw a transient 401 from our auth service (token rotation) and rewrote the upstream host to ui-host. That's a logic bug.

maria: Root cause summary: transient upstream 502 + auth rotation causing auth middleware to treat API call as browser session -> UI fallback handler returned HTML 200. Exposed because strict JSON enforcement was not applied on that fallback path.

aj: Customer looking for compensation for tokens consumed during failures. Support asked billing-team to review.

sam: Patch landed to prevent UI fallback for API routes and to enforce JSON error output when response_format=structured. Deployed to canary.

devin: Regression tests added + alert created. I'll schedule a follow-up run to validate after 24h.

maria: Closing loop: will update customer once canary stable. Thanks all. :tada:

aj: Thx!
